Hi Marcus / Sofia,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We shared the draft SOW with our procurement team and they have two pushbacks before legal will clear: 1) the early termination language — they want clearer bounds on credits if we downsize within the first 12 months; and 2) the ramp schedule — they want an opt-out window after an initial ramp, but only if there are firm downsell protections so Redwood doesn’t absorb open-ended risk.

Could you outline the maximum credit exposure and propose a staged ramp schedule (months 1–6) that gives us an opt-out without excessive credits? Also attaching the version of the SOW we returned with inline notes (Clearspring_SOW_v2_redlines.pdf).

We are aiming to sign by mid-April pending this language.

Hi Maya — appreciate the clarity and the redlines.

High-level proposal (internal summary for now, will follow with updated contract language):
- Staged ramp: 0–3 months pilot at 40% committed capacity, months 4–6 step up to 75% committed; after month 6 customer may elect an opt-out with a defined credit schedule.
- Downsell protection / early-exit credits: if customer opts out between months 7–12, Redwood provides a pro-rated credit equal to unused committed spend less a 25% risk allowance (i.e., credit = unused committed spend * 75%). Credits expire after 12 months.
- If customer reduces committed capacity but stays on platform, we allow a single "staged downsell" (one step down) with 60 days notice and a one-time fee to cover provisioning delta.

I want to route this to Deal Desk for formal approval on the credit cap and the 25% buffer. Priyom — can you confirm whether the proposed credit multiplier and the opt-out window are approvable without exec sign-off, or should this go to Sean?

Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marcus / Sofia — routing to Deal Desk for decisioning. Summary and recommended edits below (see inline):

Summary of customer ask: opt-out after initial ramp (post-month-6) with a credit schedule for unused committed spend; wants clarity on the maximum exposure. They also asked for a single-step downsell allowance.

Deal Desk recommended guardrails (proposed contract language to include):
1) Credit cap: absolute cap at 6 months of committed MRR (this caps Redwood exposure regardless of unused spend).
2) Credit formula: prorated unused committed spend * 65% (we absorb 65%, customer retains 35% as benefit of early termination).
3) Opt-out window: customer can give 60 days notice any time after month 6 but before month 12; opt-out becomes effective at month boundary and triggers the credit calculation.
4) Staged downsell: allow one downsell event after month 6 with 90 days notice; change fee equal to one-month committed MRR to cover reprovisioning.
5) Audit and data retention: customer may request usage logs for reconciliation; Redwood will provide up to 3 months of detailed token/throughput records.

Rationale: the 6-month absolute cap protects our fiscal exposure while the 65% absorb rate leaves room for negotiation and is standard for midsize deals. The 90-day tear-down notice and change fee mitigate churn-induced operational churn.

Approvals required: because we are proposing an absolute cap (6 months of MRR) and altered credit absorption, I recommend exec approval for discounts/credit policy here. Requesting Sean for final sign-off.

Attaching suggested contract redlines (Contract_Clean_v3.pdf) for legal.

-Priyom
Deal Desk Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clearspring evaluation — early-exit and ramp details — Deal Desk review

Thanks for the write-up and the redlines. I approve the Deal Desk recommended structure with two small edits for commercial safety:

- Change the credit absorb rate to 60% (Redwood absorbs 60%, customer forfeits 40%) — this reduces exposure slightly versus 65%.
- Add a hard floor: minimum retained revenue of one month of committed MRR (i.e., even if calculated credit would be lower, we retain at least one month of revenue).

Other items (no change): 6-month absolute cap, 60-day opt-out notice window (effective after month 6), one permitted downsell with 90-day notice and one-month change fee, and logs for reconciliation (3 months).

Marcus — communicate approved language to the customer and attach the Contract_Clean_v3.pdf with the Sean-approved edits. Keep me in the loop on any counter-pressure from procurement on the absorb rate or the hard floor.

Sean Gallagher
VP, Sales — Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference
